title: State and enforce the invariant that redirect()/revalidatePath() live OUTSIDE the withTenantScope body
why_open: apps/web/src/lib/tenant-scope.ts:409-418 defines `withTenantScope` and its doc comment (lines 382-408) says the wrapper must enclose ALL of the body — and says nothing about Next.js control-flow throws. Nothing anywhere in the repo states or enforces the rule: grep for `NEXT_REDIRECT`, `isRedirectError`, `unstable_rethrow` over apps/web/src and tests/ returns zero hits. I walked every `withTenantScope(`/`withSystemTenantScope(`/`runInTenantScope(` body with a paren-matching scanner: 61 scope bodies across 38 files contain a `redirect(`, `revalidatePath(` or `notFound(` call. Server-action examples with the exact shape the review names: apps/web/src/app/(app)/messages/actions.ts:135 (scope opened :73), :190 (:142), :224 (:197), :255 (:231), :319 (:262 — the body that runs a 4-statement `db.$transaction` at :286-315), apps/web/src/app/(app)/calendar/actions.ts:166-168 (scope :25), apps/web/src/app/(app)/admin/actions.ts:73 (scope :66), :499-501 (:452), :896-898 (:879), :920 (:904), :942 (:926), :965 (:948), apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[slug]/documents/actions.ts:113 (scope :89) and :214 (:191), apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[slug]/finance/actions.ts:489-490 (scope :332), apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/actions.ts:46/102-104/142-144/159-161, apps/web/src/app/(app)/feed/actions.ts:51/84/154/233, apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[slug]/members/actions.ts:121/189, apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[slug]/memory/actions.ts:62, apps/web/src/app/(app)/resources/actions.ts:68-69/85-86, apps/web/src/app/(app)/settings/actions.ts:164/190, apps/web/src/app/(app)/messages/actions.ts:369-371. HONEST QUALIFIER, do not overstate it in the ledger: I also walked every `$transaction(` callback body in apps/web/src and found ZERO redirect/revalidatePath inside one, so today the throw always escapes after the transaction has committed. The defect that is open is the missing invariant and the missing guard — 61 sites are one added `await db.…create()` (or one `db.$transaction(async () => withTenantScope(...))` wrapper) away from the silent rollback, and nothing would catch it.
smallest_real_change: (1) Write the invariant into apps/web/src/lib/tenant-scope.ts's `withTenantScope` doc block and add a runtime guard in `runInTenantScope` (apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/context.ts:84) that inspects a thrown error's `digest` for `NEXT_REDIRECT`/`NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK` and, when the scope body was entered from inside a Prisma interactive transaction, rethrows a TenantContextError naming the file — detect the transaction with an AsyncLocalStorage flag set by a thin `withTenantTransaction()` helper rather than by sniffing Prisma internals. (2) Hoist the 61 occurrences: make each scope body RETURN what the navigation needs (`const slug = await withTenantScope(userId, async () => { ...; return club.slug })`) and put `revalidatePath(...)`/`redirect(...)` on the lines AFTER the closing `})`. Skip apps/web/src/app/(app)/approvals/actions.ts — another run owns it; leave those two sites and say so. (3) Add tests/architecture/redirect-outside-tenant-scope.test.mjs: paren-match every `withTenantScope(`/`withSystemTenantScope(`/`runInTenantScope(` body over `git ls-files 'apps/web/src/**/*.ts*'` and fail listing any body containing `redirect(`/`revalidatePath(`/`revalidateTag(`, with an allowlist keyed by file:line for the approvals files this run may not touch. MUTATION PROOF: move the `redirect` at messages/actions.ts back inside the scope body, run `node --test tests/architecture/redirect-outside-tenant-scope.test.mjs`, confirm RED naming that file:line, restore, confirm GREEN. (4) Prove the rollback is real, not assumed, in apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/isolation.itest.ts against the running Postgres: open a scope, run `db.$transaction` that creates a FeedPost then throws an error carrying `digest = 'NEXT_REDIRECT;replace;/feed;307;'`, catch it outside, assert the row is absent. That test is what makes the guard's claim checkable.

title: No React.cache()d function may return tenant rows — viewerTimeZone() violates it today
why_open: REVIEW-FINDINGS.md:54 requires the invariant be stated; it is stated nowhere and one production function breaks it. apps/web/src/lib/institution-time.ts:30-44 `export const viewerTimeZone = cache(async (userId: string) => ...)` is memoized on userId ALONE and at :37-42 reads `db.organization.findFirst(...)` — `Organization` is in TENANT_SCOPED (apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/registry.ts:31), so the value returned is derived from a tenant row that the extension (apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/extension.ts:76-77) filtered using whichever scope happened to be open on the FIRST call in that request. It also ignores the acting tenant entirely — it picks `ctx.institutionRoles[0]` (institution-time.ts:32-33), not `currentScope().institutionId` — so a user who switched institutions renders every instant in their other tenant's zone. The same file's `institutionTimeZone` (:17) is safe only because its cache key IS the institutionId. `apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/locale-cookie.ts:67 documentLocalization = cache(async () => ...)` takes NO key at all and resolves a tenant slug; it is currently safe only because a Next request renders one document, which is an accident of the caller, not a property of the function. Nothing tests any of this: grep `cache(` across apps/web/src/**/*.test.ts returns zero.
smallest_real_change: Make the tenant part of the cache key rather than removing the cache. In apps/web/src/lib/institution-time.ts change `viewerTimeZone` to take the acting institution — `export const viewerTimeZone = cache(async (userId: string, institutionId: string) => institutionTimeZone(institutionId))` — and fix every construction site in the same change (grep `viewerTimeZone(`: it is called from the calendar/dashboard/feed/messages page bodies, all of which already sit inside `withTenantScope` and have `scope.institutionId` in hand; a caller that does not can read `requireTenantScope('viewerTimeZone').institutionId`). Do NOT make the new parameter optional — an optional tenant key is invisible to tsc and reintroduces the exact bug. Then add tests/architecture/cache-does-not-cross-tenant-scopes.test.mjs asserting that every `cache(` in apps/web/src whose body mentions a TENANT_SCOPED model name (read the list from apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/registry.ts, do not re-list it) declares a parameter named institutionId/tenantId. MUTATION PROOF ON THE PRODUCER, not the helper: in apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/isolation.itest.ts, seed two institutions with different `timeZone` values and one user holding a seat in both, then within a single process call `withTenantScope(user, () => viewerTimeZone(user, scope.institutionId))` for A and then for B and assert the two zones differ; revert viewerTimeZone to the userId-only key and confirm that assertion REDS (it returns A's zone twice), restore, confirm green.

title: Provider/domain events converge without duplicate business effects — the outbox is written and never dispatched
why_open: The convergence mechanism exists as a library with ZERO production callers. apps/web/src/lib/outbox/outbox.ts:140 `dispatchOnce`, :212 `replay`, :86-106 `OutboxPorts` and :251 `RETRYABLE_STATES` are referenced only by apps/web/src/lib/outbox/outbox.test.ts (grep `dispatchOnce|claimDue|OutboxPorts` across apps/, packages/ and tools/ returns 25 hits, every one of them in that test file or in outbox.ts itself). No Prisma implementation of `OutboxPorts` exists anywhere. Rows ARE being written: apps/web/src/app/(app)/approvals/actions.ts:154-155 writes `tx.outboxEvent.create({ data: outboxEventRow({...}) })` inside the decision transaction and :436-437 does it again. apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma:1088-1119 gives OutboxEvent the full `state`/`attempts`/`lastError`/`availableAt`/`deadLetteredAt` machinery and an `@@index([state, availableAt])` described in its own comment as "the dispatcher's only query" — and there is no dispatcher. apps/web/src/app/api/jobs/ contains exactly one route (`reminders/`). So every approval decision since the outbox landed has enqueued a row that will sit at `state='pending'` forever: nothing converges, nothing dead-letters, `replay()` has no operator surface. docs/implementation/global-engine-execution-ledger.md:775-786 nonetheless marks GE-021-006 PASS for "idempotent event dispatch, retries, DLQ, replay and traceability".
smallest_real_change: Add apps/web/src/lib/outbox/prisma-ports.ts implementing `OutboxPorts` against `db`, with `claimDue` as a genuinely atomic claim — `db.$queryRaw` doing `UPDATE "OutboxEvent" SET state='dispatching', attempts=attempts+0 WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM "OutboxEvent" WHERE state IN ('pending','dispatching') AND "availableAt" <= $1 ORDER BY "availableAt" LIMIT $2 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) RETURNING *` — because a read-then-write claim lets two dispatchers take the same row and turns bounded at-least-once into unbounded. Add apps/web/src/app/api/jobs/outbox/route.ts modelled line-for-line on apps/web/src/app/api/jobs/reminders/route.ts: same `JOB_SECRET` bearer check (reminders/route.ts:71-79), same `parseJobRequest` envelope, and `forEachInstitution('outbox-dispatch', ...)` from apps/web/src/lib/tenant-scope.ts:456 so each pass runs inside one tenant's scope and the extension filters `OutboxEvent` (it is TENANT_SCOPED, registry.ts:25-27) — a dispatcher reading across tenants is the leak that registry comment already warns about. `deliver` starts as the in-process domain handler (the only consumer that exists); do NOT invent an SQS transport. MUTATION PROOF, on the producer: add apps/web/src/lib/outbox/dispatch.itest.ts against the running Postgres — seed two institutions, insert one pending OutboxEvent in each, POST the route with the job secret, assert BOTH reach `state='dispatched'` and that a second POST dispatches zero (idempotence). Then (a) change `claimDue`'s SQL to drop `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and run two concurrent POSTs — the duplicate-delivery assertion reds; (b) swap `markDispatched` to run before `deliver` and confirm the lost-record assertion reds. Restore, confirm green. Finally correct docs/implementation/global-engine-execution-ledger.md:775 — its evidence block claims dispatch that did not exist.

title: No existing connector or AI capability is overstated — three live overstatements, none of them tested against
why_open: The gate has no test and the repo currently fails it in three places. (1) apps/web/src/lib/calendar-sync.ts:15-34 declares `CalendarSyncProvider` with `push`/`pull`, a `calendarSync()` accessor and `setCalendarSyncProvider()`, and its header (:5-13) claims "When Microsoft Graph credentials are provided, a real two-way GraphCalendarSync implements the CalendarSyncProvider below and drops in with no change to callers" — grep `calendarSync\(\)|setCalendarSyncProvider|CalendarSyncProvider` across apps/ and packages/ returns SIX hits, all six inside calendar-sync.ts itself. There are no callers to be unchanged; the only implementation, `IcsFeedSync` (:24-26), implements neither method. (2) apps/web/src/components/CalendarSubscribe.tsx:82-84 tells a user "Two-way sync (edits made in Outlook flowing back into Tenure) turns on once your institution connects Microsoft 365" — nothing in the product connects Microsoft 365, and packages/provisioning/src/catalogs.ts:659-662 `CATALOG_ENTRIES` contains exactly one connector (`tenure.relay-anthropic`, :631) plus the model catalog. (3) The entire OIDC authorization-code flow in packages/identity — `beginAuthorization` (authorization-request.ts:236), `bindCallback` (:340), `exchangeCode` (code-exchange.ts:105) — has zero production callers (grep across apps/ and packages/ excluding tests: only the definitions and the re-exports at packages/identity/src/index.ts:197,198,414). apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts:3-4 signs people in with NextAuth's Okta and Credentials providers, which own their own state/PKCE handling. By contrast catalogs.ts:620-658 shows what honest looks like: the one real connector carries no certification and the gate refuses it `uncertified`.
smallest_real_change: Delete the three dead declarations in apps/web/src/lib/calendar-sync.ts:15-34 (`CalendarSyncProvider`, `IcsFeedSync`, `calendarSync`, `setCalendarSyncProvider`) and the header sentence that describes a drop-in that has nowhere to drop into; keep `calendarToken`/`verifyCalendarToken`/the ICS generator, which do have callers (apps/web/src/app/api/calendar/ics/[token]/route.ts). Then add a `PLANNED` entry to packages/provisioning/src/catalogs.ts for `microsoft.graph-calendar` so the unbuilt pack is a declared, refused row rather than a UI sentence — see WRK-100-003, which adds the lifecycle value; give it `restrictions.disclaimer` saying no two-way sync exists. Add tests/architecture/no-overstated-connectors.test.mjs that (a) scans git-tracked .ts/.tsx under apps/web/src and apps/system-studio/src for user-facing provider names (Microsoft 365, Outlook two-way, Google Workspace, Slack, Zoom, Notion, Box, Dropbox) in JSX text and template strings, and fails unless the name resolves to a CATALOG_ENTRIES key whose `availabilityDecisions(...)` verdict is `available`, and (b) fails on any exported symbol in apps/web/src/lib whose doc comment claims a caller when `git grep` finds none. MUTATION PROOF: re-add the `CalendarSyncProvider` interface and confirm (b) reds; point (a)'s allowlist at a fabricated `slack` claim string in a test fixture file and confirm it reds naming the file:line; restore both. NOTE FOR THE IMPLEMENTER: apps/web/src/components/CalendarSubscribe.tsx:82-84 is the third overstatement and apps/web/src/components is owned by another cluster run — leave the file untouched, let the new test RED on it, and record it in the ledger entry as the one blocked line with the exact string, rather than weakening the test to make it pass.

title: Prove the model cannot choose tenant, token, provider account, unchecked recipient, or unrestricted operation
why_open: There is no invocation boundary to prove anything about. apps/web/src/lib/relay-tools.ts:81-126 `authorizeRelayTools` builds a real `{ offered, refused }` decision per tool per principal, and its single production consumer collapses it to a boolean: apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:99-102 does `const tools = authorizeRelayTools(...)`, `const mayRetrieve = toolOffered(tools, 'search.corpus')`, then calls `rankDocs(await loadSearchCorpus(userId), ...)` DIRECTLY — the authorized `ToolRegistration` (its `readOnly`, its `requiredPermission`, its `reauthorizesPerCall`) never reaches the call that does the work. There is no function anywhere that takes a model-proposed tool name and arguments: `aiComplete` (apps/web/src/lib/ai.ts:94-99) accepts two strings and a token budget, sends no `tools` array to the vendor (ai.ts:101-107), and its return value is rendered as prose. So today "the model cannot choose an operation" is true only because tool-calling was never wired — an accident of the current shape, not a property the code holds, and there is no test asserting any of it (grep `tenantId` / `recipient` across apps/web/src/lib/relay-tools.test.ts: zero hits; the file tests offered/refused only). modules/index.ts:464-473 registers exactly ONE tool, read-only, so the moment a second, writing tool is added there is nothing between the model's output and the write.
smallest_real_change: Add `invokeRelayTool(set: RelayToolset, context: TenantContext, proposal: { toolKey: string; args: Record<string, unknown> })` to apps/web/src/lib/relay-tools.ts as the single door, returning a discriminated `{ ok: true; tool; args }` | `{ ok: false; refusal }`, and make apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:99-102 go through it instead of `toolOffered` + a direct `rankDocs` call. Four refusals, each with a named reason: (a) `toolKey` not in `set.offered`; (b) `args` contains any of `tenantId`/`institutionId`/`connectionId`/`accountId`/`apiKey`/`onBehalfOf` — the tenant and the provider account come from `context.tenantId` and from process configuration, never from the proposal, so a proposed key is a refusal and not a silent overwrite; (c) `tool.readOnly === false` without an explicit human-confirmation token argument; (d) a recipient-bearing argument (`to`/`cc`/`bcc`/`recipients`) that is not a subset of a caller-supplied allowed set. Keep `toolOffered` as the read-side predicate; do not widen `ToolRegistration` (packages/contracts is owned by another run). MUTATION PROOF ON THE PRODUCER, not the helper — assert on what the ROUTE emits: add a route test that posts a chat request whose body carries `{ toolKey: 'search.corpus', args: { tenantId: '<other institution>' } }`, and assert the JSON response's `toolRefusal` names the refused argument and that the returned `sources` are the acting tenant's rows. Then delete the `tenantId` case from (b), confirm that route test reds; then make `invokeRelayTool` accept an unoffered toolKey, confirm the refusal test reds. Restore both.

title: Bind exact provider packs to capability and industry requirements from the catalog; unbuilt packs remain PLANNED
why_open: Neither half exists. (1) There is no `PLANNED` lifecycle: packages/provisioning/src/catalogs.ts:54-66 declares `CatalogLifecycle` as DRAFT|SUBMITTED|CERTIFIED|PUBLISHED|DEPRECATED|REVOKED, and `LIFECYCLE_TRANSITIONS` (:68-79) has no entry point for a pack somebody intends to build but has not started — `DRAFT` is documented as "Being written", which is a different fact from "planned, nobody has started". (2) Nothing binds a pack to a capability or industry requirement: `CatalogEntry`/`ConnectorEntry` (catalogs.ts:194-199) carry key, displayName, lifecycle, publisher, egressHosts, compatibility, certification, restrictions — and no requirement ids. grep `requirementId|WRK-|capabilityRequirement` across packages/provisioning/src returns zero. So `CATALOG_ENTRIES` (:659-662) is one connector plus the model catalog with no line back to the WRK-080/090/100 requirements that name Microsoft, Google, Slack, Zoom, Notion, Box, Dropbox, Jira, Confluence, Asana, Monday, Linear, ClickUp, Trello, Smartsheet, Airtable, Coda, Miro, Webex, RingCentral, DocuSign, Adobe Sign, Egnyte and ShareFile — 24 named packs, none of which appear anywhere in the codebase as any kind of declared row. The production caller that would render them already exists: apps/system-studio/src/app/page.tsx:71-73 splits `availabilityDecisions(CATALOG_ENTRIES, availabilityScope)` into offered/refused.
smallest_real_change: Add `PLANNED` as the first `CatalogLifecycle` value in packages/provisioning/src/catalogs.ts:54 with transitions `PLANNED: ['DRAFT', 'REVOKED']`, and make `isUsable`/`availabilityDecisions` refuse it with reason `planned` (the same shape as the existing `uncertified` refusal at :450-475) so a PLANNED pack renders under `refused` in apps/system-studio/src/app/page.tsx:73 rather than being invisible. Add packages/provisioning/src/provider-packs.ts declaring the 24 named packs as `ConnectorEntry` rows at `lifecycle: 'PLANNED'`, each with a `requirementIds: readonly string[]` naming the exact WRK requirement that asks for it (`microsoft.outlook-mail` -> WRK-080-001, `zoom.meetings` -> WRK-090-002, `atlassian.jira` -> WRK-100-001, …), and append them to `CATALOG_ENTRIES`. Put `requirementIds` on the new rows only via a `ProviderPackEntry extends ConnectorEntry` in the new file — do NOT add it to `CatalogEntry`, because `MODEL_CATALOG` is constructed in packages/platform-config which another run owns, and a required field there would not compile. Export both from packages/provisioning/src/index.ts. Add tests/architecture/provider-packs-bind-requirements.test.mjs asserting every `requirementIds` entry is a real id in docs/architecture/capability-completeness-registry.yaml and that every pack whose requirement is not PASS in the ledger is `PLANNED`. MUTATION PROOF: set `microsoft.outlook-mail` to `PUBLISHED` and confirm the new test reds (its requirement WRK-080-001 is FAIL); separately point one `requirementIds` at `WRK-999-999` and confirm the id check reds; then delete the `planned` branch from `availabilityDecisions` and confirm the system-studio catalog test — which must assert on what `availabilityDecisions` RETURNS for a planned entry, not on `isUsable` called directly — reds. Restore all three.

title: Test OAuth CSRF/mix-up/code-interception/token-substitution/wrong-account/confused-deputy and refresh-token theft/reuse
why_open: Four of the eight attack classes have no check to test, and the flow they would test has no production caller. packages/identity/src/authorization-request.ts:340-374 `bindCallback` refuses UNKNOWN_TRANSACTION / ALREADY_USED / EXPIRED / STATE_MISMATCH / WRONG_CONNECTION — good CSRF and single-use coverage — but `CallbackInput` (:325-330) is `{ state, connectionId, at }`: the transaction carries `tenantId` (:162) and it is NEVER compared, so a callback delivered against another tenant's request passes every check (WRONG-TENANT). There is no browser or session binding at all — no `sessionId`/`browserBindingDigest` on `AuthorizationTransaction` (:159-176) and no cookie compared in `bindCallback` — so a transaction started in the attacker's browser and completed in the victim's is accepted (WRONG-USER / login-CSRF). grep `mix.?up|confused.?deputy|token.?substitut|refresh.?token` across packages/identity/src returns zero hits in production code and zero in the 22 test files; `exchangeCode` (code-exchange.ts:105-172) has no issuer-binding check and there is no refresh-token module in the package at all (`ls packages/identity/src | grep refresh` is empty), so reuse-detection cannot be tested because it does not exist. And nothing routes through any of it: `beginAuthorization`, `bindCallback` and `exchangeCode` have zero callers outside packages/identity (apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts:3-4 signs in via NextAuth's Okta and Credentials providers).
smallest_real_change: Close the two missing checks before writing the tests, or the tests prove nothing. (1) In packages/identity/src/authorization-request.ts widen `CallbackInput` (:325) to `{ state, connectionId, tenantId, browserBindingDigest, at }` and add two refusals to `CallbackRefusal` (:295-300): `WRONG_TENANT` when `transaction.tenantId !== callback.tenantId`, and `WRONG_BROWSER` when a new required `browserBindingDigest` on `AuthorizationTransaction` (:159) does not match — both compared with the existing constant-time `digestsEqual`, both returning `SAFE_CALLBACK_MESSAGE` so which check fired stays out of the response. THIS WIDENS TWO TYPES: fix every construction site in the same change — `BeginInput` (:208-232) and `beginAuthorization`'s returned transaction (:236-292) must carry the digest, and packages/identity/src/federation-e2e.test.ts plus authorization-request.test.ts build transactions by hand; make the field REQUIRED so tsc finds them rather than optional, which would compile everywhere and fail only at runtime. (2) Add packages/identity/src/refresh-rotation.ts: a pure `rotateRefreshToken({ presented, storedFamily, at })` returning `ROTATED` | `REUSE_DETECTED` (which revokes the whole family, the standard response to theft), exported from index.ts. (3) Then the tests, one per named class, in authorization-request.test.ts / code-exchange.test.ts / refresh-rotation.test.ts. MUTATION PROOF, one per check: delete the tenantId comparison and confirm the wrong-tenant test reds; delete the browser-binding comparison and confirm the wrong-user test reds; make `rotateRefreshToken` return ROTATED for an already-redeemed token and confirm the reuse test reds. Restore each. State honestly in the ledger that this hardens the SSO-inbound primitives and that the OUTBOUND connector OAuth of WRK-040-001/004 does not exist yet, so those attack classes remain FAIL rather than being claimed by proxy.

title: Run restore, provider outage, token compromise, webhook flood, stale ACL, poisoned content and cross-tenant incident exercises
why_open: Seven exercises are named; the repo runs at most one and a half of them. apps/web/src/lib/jobs/ contains exactly one file, reminders-isolation.itest.ts — a cross-tenant check for one job. There is no exercise directory and no runbook: grep `incident|runbook|game.?day|tabletop` across apps/web/src, packages/ and tools/ returns nothing operational. Concretely, per class: RESTORE — no per-tenant restore drill exists (REVIEW-FINDINGS.md:59 flags this and asks for a gate with a runbook). PROVIDER OUTAGE — apps/web/src/lib/ai.ts:112-142 retries once on 429/529 then degrades to null, and nothing tests that path end-to-end from the route. TOKEN COMPROMISE — apps/web/src/lib/calendar-sync.ts:44-58 mints and verifies an HMAC calendar token derived from `AUTH_SECRET` with NO expiry, no revocation and no rotation story, and there is no exercise that rotates the secret and proves outstanding feeds stop resolving. WEBHOOK FLOOD — apps/web/src/app/api/jobs/reminders/route.ts:71-79 authenticates with a bearer secret and has no rate limit, no concurrency bound and no overlap guard, and no test posts it concurrently. STALE ACL — apps/web/src/lib/relay-tools.ts:31-36 documents `reauthorizesPerCall` as the defence, and no test revokes a seat mid-session and re-asks. POISONED CONTENT — apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:126-129 concatenates tenant document bodies into the prompt with no delimiter or escaping, and client-supplied `history` turns at :131-136, with no injection exercise. CROSS-TENANT — apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/isolation.itest.ts is real and is the one to extend.

Build the three that exercise real code paths and mark the other four BLOCKED_EXTERNAL naming the commands that would unblock them (restore needs an RDS snapshot restore against a side instance; provider outage needs a vendor sandbox).
